environment.gateway: https://lgw.gru.ai/v1 (live arms) + mock anthropic upstream (wire arms)
environment.wire_arms: in-process envelope + ThreadingHTTPServer mock upstream returning anthropic content-block replies

goal: Reproduce and attribute the reported symptom: after installing keysmith, Codex stops calling tools.

A_direct_contract.deployment: model_instructions_file = ./gpt-unrestricted.md (v0.6.0 unrestricted preset), direct lgw gateway

probe_list_and_read.note: single-turn ls+read task: contract did not suppress tools here

probe_edit_and_verify.note: multi-turn edit-verify loop intact under contract on this gateway/day

C_stock_baseline.deployment: no instructions file, direct lgw gateway

probe_list_and_read.symptom: turn.failed after reconnect loop; codex stderr: 'Reconnecting... unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway: upstream reply has no choices'

root_cause_1.finding: translate_response only decoded chat.completion shape (choices[].message.tool_calls). An anthropic-shape reply (content blocks + tool_use + stop_reason) raised EnvelopeError 'upstream reply has no choices' and the tool call was dropped entirely.
root_cause_1.fix: shape-sniffing _extract_output: anthropic content-block decode first (text blocks join to message; tool_use blocks become custom_tool_call items; stop_reason tool_use/end_turn map to completed), chat.completion decode retained as fallback

probe_tool_roundtrip_after_fix_1.symptom: infinite loop: 4400+ identical item.completed agent_message events; codex stderr repeated 'unsupported custom tool call: shell'

root_cause_2.finding: two compounding wire mismatches: (a) the mock's hardcoded tool name 'shell' was not in Codex's declared tool set (declared: exec/custom, wait/function, request_user_input/function, collaboration/namespace) - codex router rejects unknown custom tool names; (b) after a correctly-named tool call executed, Codex sent its result as a custom_tool_call_output item (NOT function_call_output), which translate_request dropped through to an empty user text message - the model never saw the tool result and re-emitted the same assistant message forever.
root_cause_2.fix: (a) confirmed wire contract by echoing the declared tool name from the translated anthropic tools array; (b) translate_request now maps item type custom_tool_call_output to a user tool_result block, and _tool_output_text decodes the list-of-input_text-blocks output shape

wire_evidence: r2-1.json: round 1 raw Responses request (additional_tools + developer/user messages)
r2-2.json: round 2 raw Responses request carrying custom_tool_call + custom_tool_call_output history
raw-1.json: stock tool declaration capture (4 tools: exec/wait/request_user_input/collaboration)
probe_list_and_read.outcome: exit=0; two rounds: assistant message + custom_tool_call -> tool executed -> custom_tool_call_output -> tool_result -> final answer 'The first line is: alpha 1'; no loop, no reconnect

probe_tool_execution_e2e.finding: the phase-0 e2e "round trip" converged messages but never executed a command: item.completed held only agent_messages. Live-gateway capture (20 requests) showed every custom_tool_call output "SyntaxError: Unexpected token :". Root cause: _translate_tools declares input_schema {input: string}, so the upstream emits tool_use input {"input": "<raw js>"}; the return path passed the JSON envelope through as custom_tool_call.input, but Codex grammars expect RAW source (JS for exec). Fixed by _unwrap_tool_input on the anthropic decode path plus a JSON-envelope unwrap on the chat.completion emission path.
probe_tool_execution_e2e.outcome: exit=0; one real command_execution (ls + sed) through envelope -> live gateway; final answer correct; single round, no loop

secondary_fixes.max_tokens: translate_request default max_tokens 4096 -> 16384 (tool-call turns carry full working output; 4096 truncates agentic sessions mid-call)
secondary_fixes.usage_normalization: usage decode now accepts both prompt_tokens/completion_tokens (chat) and input_tokens/output_tokens (anthropic)

conclusions: The reported 'Codex does not call tools after install' has two independent transport-layer causes when the envelope path is active, both now fixed and pinned by tests; the direct-deployment path did not reproduce tool suppression on this gateway/day (both probes passed under the v0.6.0 contract), so the dominant real-world failure was the envelope return path. A third compounding cause (JSON-envelope vs raw-grammar mismatch) was found in live e2e and fixed with _unwrap_tool_input.

Prompt-side tool-affirmation (Layer EXECUTE in the planned overlay preset) remains scheduled for Phase 1 as defense-in-depth; wire evidence shows Codex 0.144.6 declares its tools via additional_tools items and expects custom_tool_call/custom_tool_call_output round-trips.
SSE is completed-frame full replay; incremental streaming remains Phase 2 work. Codex tolerates full replay (both e2e and live mock runs converged with stream:true).
